title: Rollout variant: screen-reader semantics, keyboard flow, and i18n-ready contrast tokens
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket covers a UX pattern update for rollout variant controls in the Console: making variant labels and selection states reliably announceable to screen readers, ensuring keyboard-only workflows map to a predictable focus order across localized label lengths, and adopting contrast token fallbacks that work for translations (longer text, different punctuation). The goal is to ship a small prototype and an accessibility spec that engineering can implement across the Rollouts/Variant inspector and the compact variant chooser used in cost view rollouts.
background: Users running canary and A/B rollouts rely on a compact variant chooser that currently renders visual chips with icons and terse labels. Accessibility testing and internal bug reports found: (1) screen readers read sibling content out of order when variant chips are rendered in a flex-wrapped container; (2) keyboard focus jumps unpredictably when localized labels wrap onto multiple lines; (3) contrast tokens used for variant states (active/disabled/hover) fall below AA when labels expand in some locales; (4) pluralization in status microcopy causes inconsistent ARIA live updates across locales. We need a robust, locale-ready pattern that preserves the compact UI while meeting WCAG 2.1 AA and i18n constraints.
proposed_changes: Introduce an explicit semantic container role (region + aria-labelledby) around the variant list to stabilize screen-reader reading order and provide a short context label per container.
Replace implicit visual-only chips with <button> semantics and add aria-pressed + aria-describedby for variant status and rollout percentages.
Define a keyboard focus model: arrow-left/right to move selection; tab to leave the list; shift-tab to move backward. Ensure focus index persists when DOM reflows due to translations.
Add an offscreen live region pattern for status updates with locale-aware pluralization keys (use ICU format) to avoid repetitive or truncated announcements.

Adopt existing contrast tokens but add a localized-length test harness; if contrast drops below 4.5:1 for body text at the longest translation provided, fall back to a stronger token and use layered outline for icon-only variants.
Create guidance for translators to avoid leading punctuation in labels that can change how screen readers speak a chip (e.g., no leading colon/comma).
acceptance_criteria: SR: Screen readers announce the container label then the focused variant label and status in the expected order (container -> variant -> status).
Keyboard: Left/Right arrow moves focus between variants consistently after locale-triggered reflow. Tab order leaves the list as a single group element.
Contrast: All visible text in variant states meets WCAG AA at 14px body size using the longest translation for each supported locale or falls back to approved stronger token.
Localized announcements: Status updates use ICU pluralization keys and do not produce duplicate announcements when state toggles rapidly.
Docs: Implementation PR includes a11y regression tests (axe + voiceover smoke script) and a one-page doc for translators about label constraints.
decisions: Use button semantics for each variant to preserve native keyboard behavior (decision made 2026-03-04).
Implement an aria-live polite offscreen region for percentage/status updates rather than relying on aria-pressed changes (decision made 2026-03-06).
Adopt ICU message format for all rollout microcopy to centralize pluralization logic (decision made 2026-03-07).

risks: Long translations may still push chips to multiple lines in very narrow panels; will need responsive collapse rule (component-level) — engineering effort may be non-trivial.
Adding live-announcement logic increases JS surface area for the component; requires performance testing on low-end devices to avoid jank during rapid variant updates.
Changing token fallbacks could slightly alter the visual design; product sign-off required for degraded visual variants used in strict-contrast locales.
notes: Implementation checklist: component API changes, aria attributes, focus management util, translation keys (ICU), contrast test harness, e2e a11y tests.
Follow-up: schedule paired dev/design session to validate focus persistence across DOM reconcilations (ENG-2145 + DES-864209).
If timeboxed, prioritize screen-reader announceability and keyboard flow; defer contrast fallback automation to next sprint if needed.
